text:
Both teams arrive on three-game winning streaks and both are short-handed. Toronto beat the Rangers 5-4 on Wednesday when Troy Stecher scored with 0:28 left, but it is without John Tavares (injured reserve, return estimated Nov 27). Colton Sissons has taken his spot beside Nylander and McKenna, and Gavin McKenna has moved onto the first power-play unit. Edmonton came back from two goals down to beat Carolina 6-5 in a shootout, a night Nikolaj Ehlers reached 600 career points, and it is missing Mattias Ekholm, with Jake Walman next in line for his minutes.

The chances favor Edmonton. The Oilers have the cleaner defensive numbers (2.69 expected goals against per 60, the quality of chances allowed, versus 3.47 for Toronto) and the better penalty kill. Toronto takes 4.1 penalties a game, which keeps handing out power plays. In net, projected starter Sergei Bobrovsky is +3.3 in goals saved above expected this season, while Edmonton's projected Tristan Jarry is at -3.1. Last season, both were below zero.

Connor McDavid is 94% to record a point and 46% to score, riding a 10-game point streak. Leon Draisaitl has goals in five straight, and Auston Matthews, two points shy of 800, is 37% to score. Our under-the-radar pick is Edmonton's Colton Dach, a third-liner whose shots have been dangerous lately, and Toronto gives up the sixth-most expected goals per 60. We have him at 14% to score.
